claim: Memory responses occur in the context of the overall immune state and leukocytes must interact with their microenvironment and other immune cells.
source: However, memory responses occur in the context of the overall immune state and leukocytes must interact with their microenvironment and other immune cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about how immune responses function in the manuscript.

claim: Prior immune events can shift the state of diverse cell types in barrier tissues, such as parenchymal and stromal cells, thereby establishing tissue inflammatory memory that synergizes with immune cell-mediated memory to enable rapid recall of distinct exposures.
source: Indeed, studies have shown that prior immune events can shift the state of diverse cell types in barrier tissues, such as parenchymal and stromal cells, thereby establishing tissue inflammatory memory that synergizes with immune cell-mediated memory to enable rapid recall of distinct exposures (Kazer et al., 2023; Ordovas-Montanes et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies by Kazer et al., 2023 and Ordovas-Montanes et al., 2020.

claim: Half of 12 prominent studies regarding human immune heterogeneity state recruitment was intentionally restricted to one sex or a given age range.
source: To demonstrate the relevance of this issue in the context of human immunity - half of 12 prominent studies regarding human immune heterogeneity state recruitment was intentionally restricted to one sex or a given age range, otherwise variability that is attributed to a determinant category they are uninterested in would increase, thereby decreasing power (Brodin et al., 2015; Carr et al., 2016; Lakshmikanth et al., 2020; Lee et al., 2014; O'Neill et al., 2021; Orrù et al., 2013; Patin et al., 2018; Raj et al., 2014; Randolph et al., 2021; Roederer et al., 2015; Tsang et al., 2014; Ye et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to 12 specific studies that demonstrate this pattern of restricted recruitment.

claim: Children under 5 years of age, especially infants under the age of 2, are at higher risk of complications from influenza virus infection.
source: Children under 5 years of age, especially infants under the age of 2, are at higher risk of complications (Clohisey and Baillie, 2019; Ruf and Knuf, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Clohisey and Baillie, 2019 and Ruf and Knuf, 2014.

claim: The higher risk of complications in young children is thought to be due, at least in part, to lack of pre-existing immunity and a heavy reliance on CD4 type 2 responses in children as opposed to the CD4 type 1 and CD8 T cell predominant responses in adults.
source: This is thought to be due, at least in part, to lack of pre-existing immunity and a heavy reliance on CD4 type 2 responses in children as opposed to the CD4 type 1 and CD8 T cell predominant responses in adults (Cerwenka et al., 1999; Chang et al., 2011; de Kleer et al., 2016; Dowling and Levy, 2014; Duan and Thomas, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Cerwenka et al., 1999; Chang et al., 2011; de Kleer et al., 2016; Dowling and Levy, 2014; Duan and Thomas, 2016).

claim: Compared to adults, infants and young children exhibit a hyperinflammatory cytokine profile during naturally acquired influenza infection.
source: For example, a study of naturally acquired influenza infection in humans found that, compared to adults, infants and young children exhibit a hyperinflammatory cytokine profile (Oshansky et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a study by Oshansky et al., 2014 that examined naturally acquired influenza infection.

claim: Severe influenza infection is most prevalent in adults greater than 65 years of age.
source: For adults, severe influenza infection is most prevalent in those greater than 65 years of age (Gounder and Boon, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gounder and Boon, 2019.

claim: Immunosenescence is a set of age-related changes that affect both innate and adaptive immune compartments and result in dramatic impairment of immune function, leaving older adults more susceptible to infectious diseases.
source: This is thought to be largely due to immunosenescence - a set of age-related changes that affect both innate and adaptive immune compartments. Changes include altered extracellular microenvironments, soluble factors important for leukocyte homeostasis and differentiation, and modified immune cell phenotype and functional profiles. Collectively, these changes result in dramatic impairment of immune function, leaving older adults more susceptible to infectious diseases (Bulut et al., 2020; Cunha et al., 2020; Keilich et al., 2019; Molony et al., 2018; Moreau et al., 2017; Shaw et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Bulut et al., 2020; Cunha et al., 2020; Keilich et al., 2019; Molony et al., 2018; Moreau et al., 2017; Shaw et al., 2013).

claim: General changes in innate immune cells with age include reduced chemotaxis, phagocytosis, superoxide production, receptor signal transduction, antigen presentation, and interferon production.
source: General changes in innate immune cells include, but are not limited to, reduced chemotaxis, phagocytosis, superoxide production, receptor signal transduction, antigen presentation, and interferon production (Feng et al., 2021; Keilich et al., 2019; Molony et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Feng et al., 2021; Keilich et al., 2019; Molony et al., 2018.

claim: Dendritic cells from elderly donors show impaired type I and III interferon production in response to stimulation with influenza virus.
source: Indeed, studies of dendritic cells (DCs) from elderly donors show impaired type I and III interferon production in response to stimulation with influenza virus (Prakash et al., 2013; Sridharan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies by Prakash et al., 2013 and Sridharan et al., 2011.

claim: The reduction in interferon production in elderly dendritic cells was associated with decreased phosphorylation of interferon regulatory transcription factor 7 (IRF7), decreased T cell proliferation, and CD8 T cell effector function, as measured by perforin and granzyme production.
source: This reduction was associated with decreased phosphorylation of interferon regulatory transcription factor 7 (IRF7), decreased T cell proliferation, and CD8 T cell effector function, as measured by perforin and granzyme production (Sridharan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sridharan et al., 2011 that measured these specific outcomes.

claim: General age-associated changes in adaptive immunity include decreased B cells and antibody diversity, impaired regulatory T cell function, decreased naive T cell numbers concomitant with increased memory T cells, and decreased expression of receptors important for T cell activation and/or differentiation.
source: General age-associated changes in adaptive immunity include decreased B cells and antibody diversity, impaired regulatory T cell function, decreased naive T cell numbers concomitant with increased memory T cells, and decreased expression of receptors important for T cell activation and/or differentiation (Britanova et al., 2014; Frasca et al., 2004; Fulop et al., 2017; Keilich et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Britanova et al., 2014; Frasca et al., 2004; Fulop et al., 2017; Keilich et al., 2019).

claim: Influenza-specific CD8 T cells from older donors exhibited reduced diversity in the T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, suggesting increased risk for antigenic escape.
source: For example, studies of influenza-specific CD8 T cells from older donors exhibited reduced diversity in the T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, suggesting increased risk for antigenic escape (Gil et al., 2015; Naumov et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gil et al., 2015 and Naumov et al., 2008, with an inference about the implications for antigenic escape.

claim: Age-related biological changes that impact naive and memory CD8 T cell subsets include thymic involution and decreased output of lymphoid lineage committed hematopoietic stem cells.
source: Age-related biological changes that impact these subsets include thymic involution and decreased output of lymphoid lineage committed hematopoietic stem cells (Beerman et al., 2010; den Braber et al., 2012; Elyahu and Monsonego, 2021; Palmer et al., 2018; Pang et al., 2011; Thomas et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Beerman et al., 2010; den Braber et al., 2012; Elyahu and Monsonego, 2021; Palmer et al., 2018; Pang et al., 2011; Thomas et al., 2020).

claim: Chronic infections contribute to the imbalance between naive and memory CD8 T cells, with cytomegalovirus (CMV)-induced 'memory inflation' resulting in large expansions of CMV-specific memory T cells over time.
source: Chronic infections also contribute to this imbalance, with the most well-known effect from cytomegalovirus (CMV)-induced 'memory inflation', which results in large expansions of CMV-specific memory T cells over time (Adler and Reddehase, 2019; Griessl et al., 2021; Whiting et al., 2015; Zangger and Oxenius, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Adler and Reddehase, 2019; Griessl et al., 2021; Whiting et al., 2015; Zangger and Oxenius, 2022).

claim: Aging alone, in the absence of CMV infection, does not augment memory T cell numbers in the periphery.
source: Further highlighting the significance of CMV infection in shaping the CD8 T cell compartment, one study found aging alone, in the absence of CMV infection, does not augment memory T cell numbers in the periphery (Wertheimer et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a study by Wertheimer et al., 2014.

claim: Human studies have demonstrated variation in immunophenotypes during health and immune challenge based on ancestry, with important implications for population differences in susceptibility to infection and illness outcome.
source: Human studies have demonstrated variation in immunophenotypes during health and immune challenge based on ancestry, with important implications for population differences in susceptibility to infection and illness outcome (Mangino et al., 2017; O'Neill et al., 2021; Orrù et al., 2013; Randolph et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Mangino et al., 2017; O'Neill et al., 2021; Orrù et al., 2013; Randolph et al., 2021).

claim: A child with complete loss of functional IRF7 due to inheriting two different loss-of-function mutations presented with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome during primary influenza infection.
source: An example of this was recently shown in Ciancanelli et al. where an otherwise healthy child presented with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome during primary influenza infection. The child's parents were heterozygous for two different loss-of-function mutations in the IRF7 transcription factor, thus they were able to produce enough IRF7 to prevent severe infection; however, the child inherited both mutations which led to a complete loss of functional IRF7 (Ciancanelli et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ciancanelli et al., 2015 describing a specific case study.

claim: The patient with IRF7 deficiency had leukocytes that showed impaired production of type I and III interferons in response to influenza virus, and immortalized fibroblasts from the patient showed 2-log higher influenza virus titers at 48 hr post infection relative to healthy controls.
source: Coinciding with this, the patient's leukocytes showed impaired production of type I and III interferons in response to influenza virus, and immortalized fibroblasts from the patient showed 2-log higher influenza virus titers at 48 hr post infection relative to healthy controls (Ciancanelli et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ciancanelli et al., 2015 with specific experimental data.

claim: Recent studies have identified associations between severe influenza pneumonitis and immunodeficiencies in IRF9 and TLR3.
source: Recent studies have also identified associations between severe influenza pneumonitis and immunodeficiencies in IRF9 and TLR3, further highlighting the significant impact of inborn errors of immunity in genes related to the initiation or transduction of interferon responses during influenza infection (Hernandez et al., 2018; Lim et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hernandez et al., 2018 and Lim et al., 2019.

claim: IFITM3 is an interferon-stimulated gene which has been shown to function as a viral restriction factor by blocking virus-host membrane fusion and augmenting antibody-mediated neutralization of influenza A virus.
source: IFITM3 is an interferon-stimulated gene which has been shown to function as a viral restriction factor by blocking virus-host membrane fusion and augmenting antibody-mediated neutralization of influenza A virus (Brass et al., 2009; Desai et al., 2014; Gorman et al., 2016; Lanz et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Brass et al., 2009; Desai et al., 2014; Gorman et al., 2016; Lanz et al., 2021).

claim: In populations of Asian descent, IFITM3 SNP rs12252-C has consistently been associated with severe influenza illness.
source: In populations of Asian descent, SNP rs12252-C has consistently been associated with severe influenza illness; however, studies in populations of European descent have shown low prevalence of the risk allele and mixed results regarding disease severity (Everitt et al., 2012; Yang et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Everitt et al., 2012; Yang et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2013).

claim: Studies in populations of European descent have shown low prevalence of the IFITM3 rs12252-C risk allele and mixed results regarding disease severity.
source: In populations of Asian descent, SNP rs12252-C has consistently been associated with severe influenza illness; however, studies in populations of European descent have shown low prevalence of the risk allele and mixed results regarding disease severity (Everitt et al., 2012; Yang et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Everitt et al., 2012; Yang et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2013).

claim: IFITM3 SNP rs34481144-A was enriched in severe influenza patients and prevalent in European populations.
source: In a study of three independent influenza cohorts, IFITM3 SNP rs34481144-A was enriched in severe patients and prevalent in European populations (Allen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Allen et al., 2017 with data from three cohorts.

claim: The IFITM3 SNP rs34481144 is located within the promoter region of IFITM3, and the risk allele is associated with decreased expression of IFITM3 and disrupted transcriptional correlations between IFITM3 and its neighboring genes.
source: This SNP is located within the promoter region of IFITM3, and the risk allele is associated with decreased expression of IFITM3 and disrupted transcriptional correlations between IFITM3 and its neighboring genes.
evidence: This claim is stated as a finding from the Allen et al., 2017 study mentioned in the preceding sentence.

claim: Results from luciferase reporter assays in HEK293T cells show that rs34481144 alters promoter activity and modulates reporter gene expression at baseline and in response to stimulation with poly(I:C), live influenza virus, and interferon alpha.
source: Results from luciferase reporter assays in HEK293T cells and using plasmids with a minimal promoter show that rs34481144 alters promoter activity and modulates reporter gene expression at baseline and in response to stimulation with poly(I:C), live influenza virus, and interferon alpha.
evidence: This claim describes experimental data from luciferase reporter assays.

claim: The risk genotype of IFITM3 rs12252 is always inherited with the protective genotype of rs34481144, suggesting the risk alleles are on opposite haplotypes and have independent mechanisms.
source: Importantly, this study also found that the risk genotype of rs12252 is always inherited with the protective genotype of rs34481144, suggesting the risk alleles are on opposite haplotypes and have independent mechanisms (Allen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Allen et al., 2017 with an inference about the mechanism.

claim: Para-inflammation arises from cellular stress or tissue malfunction, and is characterized by systemic low-grade inflammation, which alters homeostatic set points, and promotes the development of chronic inflammatory diseases.
source: More recently described, para-inflammation arises from cellular stress or tissue malfunction, and is characterized by systemic low-grade inflammation, which alters homeostatic set points, and promotes the development of chronic inflammatory diseases (Medzhitov, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Medzhitov, 2008.

claim: A primary driver of para-inflammation is a dysmetabolic microenvironment that is driven, at least in part, by comorbidities such as obesity, dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, and hypertension.
source: A primary driver of para-inflammation is a dysmetabolic microenvironment that is driven, at least in part, by comorbidities such as obesity, dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, and hypertension.
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge about para-inflammation.

claim: Chronic medical conditions such as obesity, dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, and hypertension are often co-occurring, have been associated with poor outcome to immune challenge, and contribute to the inflammatory state that drives the overt insulin resistance that is central to the etiopathology of metabolic syndrome.
source: These chronic medical conditions are often co-occurring, have been associated with poor outcome to immune challenge, and contribute to the inflammatory state that drives the overt insulin resistance that is central to the etiopathology of metabolic syndrome (Medzhitov, 2008; Paragh et al., 2014; Zmora et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Medzhitov, 2008; Paragh et al., 2014; Zmora et al., 2017.

claim: In mouse models of influenza infection, obese mice exhibit increased viral spread and diversity in virus quasispecies.
source: For example, in mouse models of influenza infection, obese mice exhibit increased viral spread and diversity in virus quasispecies (Honce et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Honce et al., 2020 with experimental data from mouse models.

claim: Obese host-passaged influenza viruses showed higher mutations associated with virulence and increased replication kinetics in vitro.
source: Additionally, obese host-passaged influenza viruses showed higher mutations associated with virulence and increased replication kinetics in vitro.
evidence: This claim describes experimental findings from the Honce et al., 2020 study mentioned in the preceding sentence.

claim: Differentiated normal human bronchial epithelial cells from obese hosts exhibited increased viral replication and impaired interferon responses upon infection with H1N1 influenza virus.
source: Coinciding with these results, differentiated normal human bronchial epithelial cells from obese hosts exhibited increased viral replication and impaired interferon responses upon infection with H1N1 influenza virus (Honce et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Honce et al., 2020 with experimental data from human cells.

claim: Mouse and human studies have shown that diabetics have impairments in multiple facets of innate immunity, such as in leukocyte recruitment, neutrophil reactive oxygen species production, NK cell activating receptor signaling, and monocyte/macrophage phagocytosis and cytokine production.
source: Mouse and human studies have shown that diabetics have impairments in multiple facets of innate immunity, such as in leukocyte recruitment, neutrophil reactive oxygen species production, NK cell activating receptor signaling, and monocyte/macrophage phagocytosis and cytokine production (Berbudi et al., 2020; Geerlings and Hoepelman, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Berbudi et al., 2020 and Geerlings and Hoepelman, 1999.

claim: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells from obese individuals showed reduced activation of CD8 T cells and production of effector molecules in response to stimulation or vaccination with influenza virus.
source: In support of this, impairment of T cell responses during metabolic stress has been shown for viral challenge, wherein peripheral blood mononuclear cells from obese individuals showed reduced activation of CD8 T cells and production of effector molecules in response to stimulation or vaccination with influenza virus (Paich et al., 2013; Sheridan et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Paich et al., 2013 and Sheridan et al., 2012.

claim: The antigen presentation machinery and peptidome of dendritic cells from obese mice exhibit unique and increased oxidative post-translational modifications, resulting in epitope-specific alterations in peptide presentation.
source: Indeed, the antigen presentation machinery and peptidome of DCs from obese mice exhibit unique and increased oxidative PTMs, resulting in epitope-specific alterations in peptide presentation (Clement et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Clement et al., 2021 with experimental data from mouse models.

claim: Prior infectious exposures can modulate tissue and immune compartments, resulting in altered functional responses upon subsequent homologous or heterologous infection and vaccination.
source: Prior infectious exposures can modulate tissue and immune compartments, resulting in altered functional responses upon subsequent homologous or heterologous infection and vaccination (Kazer et al., 2023; Sparks et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kazer et al., 2023 and Sparks et al., 2023.

claim: Antibodies circulate throughout the body and serve neutralizing and non-neutralizing functions that defend against influenza infection and/or severe disease.
source: Protection conferred by B cells is humoral-mediated, antibodies (secreted versions of the B cell receptor) circulate throughout the body, and serve neutralizing and non-neutralizing functions that defend against influenza infection and/or severe disease (Henry Dunand et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2016; Krammer, 2019; Ng et al., 2019; Rajendran et al., 2021; Tan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Henry Dunand et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2016; Krammer, 2019; Ng et al., 2019; Rajendran et al., 2021; Tan et al., 2016).

claim: Immunodominant targets of anti-influenza humoral immunity are often sites of mutation, which can lead to immune evasion.
source: However, immunodominant targets of anti-influenza humoral immunity are often sites of mutation, which can lead to immune evasion (Krammer, 2019; Wu and Wilson, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Krammer, 2019 and Wu and Wilson, 2017.

claim: Pre-existing anti-influenza humoral immunity can alter the breadth and quality of antibody responses to subsequent influenza challenge.
source: One challenge to the development of such vaccines is pre-existing anti-influenza humoral immunity, as most individuals acquire influenza virus multiple times throughout their lifetime and this can alter the breadth and quality of antibody responses (Neu et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Neu et al., 2016.

claim: Original antigenic sin refers to the concept that the first exposure to influenza virus infection leaves an immunological imprint that conditions immunity to subsequent influenza challenge.
source: Original antigenic sin refers to the concept that the first exposure to influenza virus infection leaves an immunological imprint that conditions immunity to subsequent influenza challenge (Francis, 1960; Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Francis, 1960 and Zhang et al., 2019.

claim: Primary addiction refers to the active suppression of de novo B cell responses by pre-existing immunity, the effects of which have been shown to be dependent on antigenic distance, such that it decreases as antigenic distance increases between priming and boosting strains.
source: Primary addiction refers to the active suppression of de novo B cell responses by pre-existing immunity, the effects of which have been shown to be dependent on antigenic distance, such that it decreases as antigenic distance increases between priming and boosting strains (Schiepers et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Schiepers et al., 2023.

claim: Epitope masking occurs when pre-existing antibodies block or sterically hinder access to antigen, thereby blunting the adaptive response due to reduced antigenic load.
source: Epitope masking occurs when pre-existing antibodies block or sterically hinder access to antigen, thereby blunting the adaptive response due to reduced antigenic load (Henry et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Henry et al., 2018.

claim: Antigenic seniority is a model in which the first influenza strain an individual is exposed to takes a 'senior' antigenic position in the humoral response, and each subsequent influenza infection is progressively 'junior'.
source: Antigenic seniority is a model in which the first influenza strain an individual is exposed to takes a 'senior' antigenic position in the humoral response, and each subsequent influenza infection is progressively 'junior' (Henry et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Henry et al., 2018.

claim: Each sequential encounter with influenza boosts the antibody response to prior influenza exposures through 'back-boosting', thus the most senior influenza strain is associated with the highest antibody titer due to the most boosting events.
source: This observation is mediated, at least in part, by 'back-boosting', wherein each sequential encounter with influenza boosts the antibody response to prior influenza exposures; thus, the most senior influenza strain is associated with the highest antibody titer due to the most boosting events (Henry et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Henry et al., 2018.

claim: Antigenic imprinting may be beneficial and can provide protection against novel strains, if the emerging influenza strain is within the same HA subtype as the first imprinting strain.
source: However, recent studies suggest that antigenic imprinting may also be beneficial and can provide protection against novel strains, if the emerging influenza strain is within the same HA subtype as the first imprinting strain (Gostic et al., 2019; Gostic et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gostic et al., 2019 and Gostic et al., 2016.

claim: T cells often target internal, conserved proteins of influenza, and thus are a strategic advantage in the establishment of heterosubtypic immunity.
source: In contrast to B cells, T cells often target internal, conserved proteins, and thus are a strategic advantage in the establishment of heterosubtypic immunity, as their cognate antigen is likely to be very similar, even across antigenically distinct strains of influenza.
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge about T cell immunity to influenza.

claim: Mice primed with H9N2 or H1N1 are protected against secondary challenge with novel H7N9 and exhibit early infiltration of CD8 T cells, reduced morbidity and mortality, pulmonary viral load, and time to viral clearance.
source: Studies in C57BL/6 mice have shown that mice primed with H9N2 or H1N1 are protected against secondary challenge with novel H7N9 and exhibit early infiltration of CD8 T cells, reduced morbidity and mortality, pulmonary viral load, and time to viral clearance (Duan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Duan et al., 2015 with experimental data from mouse models.

claim: The size of the memory CD8 T cell response was a predictor of positive outcome and modifying the size of the memory CD8 T cell pool modulated its protective effects.
source: Moreover, the size of the memory CD8 T cell response was a predictor of positive outcome and modifying the size of the memory CD8 T cell pool modulated its protective effects, highlighting the important role of CD8s in conferring heterosubtypic protection (Duan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Duan et al., 2015 with experimental data.

claim: In the influenza mouse model, CD8 T cells target PB1 (polymerase basic protein 1), PA (polymerase acidic protein), and NP (nucleoprotein).
source: In the influenza mouse model, CD8 T cells target PB1 (polymerase basic protein 1), PA (polymerase acidic protein), and NP (nucleoprotein).
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge about CD8 T cell targets in the mouse influenza model.

claim: Although both H9N2 and H1N1 ultimately conferred protection, they induced different CD8 T cell immunodominance hierarchies and differed in the degree to which they elicited beneficial outcomes.
source: Although both H9N2 and H1N1 ultimately conferred protection, they induced different CD8 T cell immunodominance hierarchies and differed in the degree to which they elicited beneficial outcomes (Duan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Duan et al., 2015 with experimental data.

claim: Resident memory T cells (TRM) are long-lived, reside in tissues without recirculation, and can confer both antigen-dependent and -independent mechanisms of protection against homologous and heterologous pathogenic challenge.
source: Resident memory T cells (TRM) are a special subset of T cells that are long-lived, reside in tissues without recirculation, and can confer both antigen-dependent and -independent mechanisms of protection against homologous and heterologous pathogenic challenge.
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge about TRM cells.

claim: Mouse studies have shown that TRM cells produce antiviral cytokines more rapidly than systemic effector memory T cells, can quickly trigger innate and adaptive immune responses, augment maturation of local DCs and NK cells, and are capable of inducing broadly active antiviral and antibacterial gene expression.
source: Specifically, mouse studies have shown that TRM cells produce antiviral cytokines more rapidly than systemic effector memory T cells, can quickly trigger innate and adaptive immune responses, augment maturation of local DCs and NK cells, and are capable of inducing broadly active antiviral and antibacterial gene expression, thereby inducing a tissue-wide 'pathogen alert' and effectively acting as alarmins (Ariotti et al., 2014; Jiang et al., 2012; McMaster et al., 2015; Pizzolla et al., 2017; Schenkel et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple mouse studies (Ariotti et al., 2014; Jiang et al., 2012; McMaster et al., 2015; Pizzolla et al., 2017; Schenkel et al., 2014).

claim: Mice co-infected with latent murine gammaherpesvirus 68 or murine cytomegalovirus (MCMV) exhibit augmented activation of APCs and altered cytokine production following secondary challenge with bacteria or influenza virus.
source: For example, mice co-infected with latent murine gammaherpesvirus 68 or murine cytomegalovirus (MCMV) exhibit augmented activation of APCs and altered cytokine production following secondary challenge with bacteria or influenza virus (Barton et al., 2007; Saito et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Barton et al., 2007 and Saito et al., 2013 with experimental data from mouse models.

claim: Co-infected mice have enhanced CD8 T cell recruitment and activation.
source: Co-infected mice also have enhanced CD8 T cell recruitment and activation, though further study is required to determine this mechanism, as well as the impact on the TCR repertoire (Saito et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Saito et al., 2013 with experimental data.

claim: Mice co-infected with MCMV and influenza exhibit higher CD8 T cell responses and decreased viral load.
source: An independent study of MCMV and influenza co-infection further supports these findings and shows that co-infected mice exhibit higher CD8 T cell responses and decreased viral load (Furman et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Furman et al., 2015 with experimental data.

claim: Memory CD8 T cells have decreased activation signal requirements to the extent that they can become activated by cytokine(s) alone or peptide concentrations as low as 1/50th of that required for stimulation of naive T cells.
source: Compared to the naive state, memory CD8 T cells have decreased activation signal requirements to the extent that they can become activated by cytokine(s) alone or peptide concentrations as low as 1/50th of that required for stimulation of naive T cells (Welsh and Selin, 2002; Youngblood et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Welsh and Selin, 2002 and Youngblood et al., 2013.

claim: Both mouse and human studies have found that influenza virus infection induces activation and expansion of non-specific memory CD8 T cells.
source: Indeed, both mouse and human studies have found that influenza virus infection induces activation and expansion of non-specific memory CD8 T cells (Sandalova et al., 2010; Sckisel et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sandalova et al., 2010 and Sckisel et al., 2014.

claim: The population of bystander-activated T cells acquires effector function that contributes to initial pathogen control and impacts disease outcome.
source: Importantly, this population of T cells acquires effector function that contributes to initial pathogen control and impacts disease outcome.
evidence: This claim is stated as an important finding from the studies mentioned in the preceding sentence.

claim: I0 is the pre-infection, overall state of the immune system, which varies across individuals and changes over time with age, new immune challenge, development of comorbidities, etc.
source: I0 is the pre-infection, overall state of the immune system, which varies across individuals and changes over time with age, new immune challenge, development of comorbidities, etc. (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is the definition of I0 provided by the authors, with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Populations with high susceptibility to influenza infection include naive infants, immunosenescent elderly, and adults with a pre-existing condition.
source: In the context of infectious challenge, there are I0 profiles associated with increased susceptibility to infection, and those associated with protection. In the case of influenza, populations with high susceptibility to infection, and thus closer to the threshold of infection, include naive infants (Figure 3B, purple cluster), immunosenescent elderly (Figure 3B, orange cluster), and adults with a pre-existing condition (Figure 3B, blue cluster).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with reference to Figure 3B showing these populations.

claim: I0 profiles associated with protection from influenza are further from the infection threshold and may represent generally healthy adults or vaccinated subjects.
source: I0 profiles associated with protection are further from the infection threshold and may represent generally healthy adults or vaccinated subjects (Figure 3B, green cluster).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The recommended modeling approach for I0 is rooted in multivariable linear or logistic regression modeling, depending on whether the outcome variable is continuous or binary, respectively.
source: The recommended modeling approach is rooted in multivariable linear or logistic regression modeling, depending on whether the outcome variable is continuous or binary, respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological recommendation provided by the authors.

claim: The set of 'core independent factors' for I0 models includes ancestry informative markers' (AIMs) principal components, age, sex, CMV status, and EBV status.
source: In the proposed framework, whether I0 is investigated as a dependent variable or utilized as an independent variable, all models contain a set of 'core independent factors' (base model, Figure 4). This includes ancestry informative markers' (AIMs) principal components, age, sex, CMV status, and EBV status.
evidence: This is a methodological recommendation provided by the authors with reference to Figure 4.

claim: Out of 39 non-genetic determinants, CMV, age, smoking, and sex were the most important non-genetic determinants of basal immune phenotypes.
source: The selection of core variables is based on an assessment of the literature on immune variation, weighting consideration of results from Patin et al., 2018, because an integrative analytical approach which spanned multiple determinant categories simultaneously was utilized, and found that out of 39 non-genetic determinants, CMV, age, smoking, and sex were the most important non-genetic determinants of basal immune phenotypes, and genetic factors primarily influenced innate cell types, whereas environmental primarily affected adaptive (Patin et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Patin et al., 2018.

claim: Genetic factors primarily influenced innate cell types, whereas environmental factors primarily affected adaptive immunity.

claim: A hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assay titer of 1:40 is associated with a 50% reduction in risk of influenza.
source: For example, a hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assay titer of 1:40 is associated with a 50% reduction in risk of influenza (Coudeville et al., 2010; Hobson et al., 1972) and would be relevant for an influenza I0 landscape, but may not be pertinent for an alternative pathogen- or immune-related illness.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Coudeville et al., 2010 and Hobson et al., 1972.

claim: Studies have shown whether a given factor affects immunity and how much can vary by immune state (basal versus acute), stimulation condition, and ethnic population.
source: Studies have shown whether a given factor affects immunity and how much can vary by immune state (basal versus acute), stimulation condition (e.g. poly(I:C) versus lipopolysaccharide), and ethnic population (Allen et al., 2017; Raj et al., 2014; Randolph et al., 2021; Randolph et al., 2021; Souquette et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Allen et al., 2017; Raj et al., 2014; Randolph et al., 2021; Randolph et al., 2021; Souquette et al., 2023).

claim: Increasing genetic diversity, rather than increasing sample size of individuals of European ancestry, improves identification of novel clinically relevant genetic loci, fine-mapping of functional variants, and portability of polygenic risk scores.
source: Indeed, recent studies have shown increasing genetic diversity, rather than increasing sample size of individuals of European ancestry, improves identification of novel clinically relevant genetic loci, fine-mapping of functional variants, and portability of polygenic risk scores (Bentley et al., 2019; Cavazos and Witte, 2021; Graham et al., 2021; Wojcik et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Bentley et al., 2019; Cavazos and Witte, 2021; Graham et al., 2021; Wojcik et al., 2019).

claim: Variation in I0 is associated with distinct immune profiles that vary in functional capacity against a given disease and are associated with different paths to disease severity.
source: The studies reviewed here provide a framework for defining the I0 and acute immune landscapes, which allows for a more comprehensive assessment of immune variation, its determinants, and how this relates to differential outcome. Taken together, it suggests and graphically represents: (1) Variation in I0 is associated with distinct immune profiles that vary in functional capacity against a given disease and are associated with different paths to disease severity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by the authors based on the reviewed literature.

claim: Multiple immunological profiles may be associated with severity of a given disease, and more unsupervised approaches are required to determine how many distinct pathophysiologies exist.
source: (2) Multiple immunological profiles may be associated with severity of a given disease, and more unsupervised approaches are required to determine how many distinct pathophysiologies exist in order to appropriately identify an optimum therapeutic target.
evidence: This is a conclusion and recommendation drawn by the authors based on the reviewed literature.

claim: A 'one-size-fits-all' approach will likely be limited in generalizability to the population as a whole, owing to unique immunophenotype groups.
source: I0 has important implications for translational and clinical research as it is commonly conducted to date. First, a 'one-size-fits-all' approach will likely be limited in generalizability to the population as a whole, owing to unique immunophenotype groups.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors based on the concept of I0 and immune variation.

claim: Equating distinct immune profiles may lead to false positive or negative associations, and could explain, at least in part, discrepancies in translating scientific findings at the bench to treatments in the clinic.
source: Second, equating distinct immune profiles, whether at the I0 state for prophylactic treatment or an acute state for therapeutic treatment, may lead to false positive or negative associations, and could explain, at least in part, discrepancies in translating scientific findings at the bench to treatments in the clinic.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors about the implications of I0 for translational research.

claim: Mathew et al. identified three cellular-based immunophenotypes associated with COVID outcome.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mathew et al., 2020 and is referenced in Figure 6.

claim: Pediatric subjects are poised for hyperresponsiveness in their immune response to influenza, whereas the elderly are poised for hyporesponsiveness.
source: In the context of I0 and influenza infection, these data suggest that the response trajectories of the immune system associated with extremes of age are distinct and opposing, such that pediatric subjects are poised for hyperresponsiveness, whereas the elderly for hyporesponsiveness - both can present a risk to the host through excessive cellular damage and impaired tissue integrity, though the former is mediated by immunopathology and the latter is damage associated with uncontrolled pathogen growth.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors based on the reviewed literature about age-related immune differences.

claim: Both hyperresponsiveness in pediatric subjects and hyporesponsiveness in elderly subjects can present a risk to the host through excessive cellular damage and impaired tissue integrity.

evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors based on the reviewed literature about age-related immune differences.

evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors based on the reviewed literature about age-related immune differences.

claim: Genetic variants that augment antiviral activity or limit proviral factors would result in a protective I0 profile.
source: Genetic variants that augment antiviral activity or limit proviral factors would result in a protective I0 profile, the converse would result in an I0 profile associated with infection or severe disease.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors about how genetic variants affect I0.

source: These studies highlight how chronic conditions can induce a dysmetabolic microenvironment that shapes I0 and can ultimately culminate in impaired immunity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by the authors based on the reviewed studies about chronic conditions.

claim: Imprinting may be detrimental if the resulting antibody repertoire is too narrow, as this provides increased opportunity for antigenic escape variants.
source: Imprinting may be detrimental if the resulting antibody repertoire is too narrow, as this provides increased opportunity for antigenic escape variants (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2019 with an inference about the implications.

claim: Shifts in the dominant HA subtypes circulating over time may underlie variation in susceptibility to novel strains in different age groups.
source: Thus, shifts in the dominant HA subtypes circulating over time may underlie variation in susceptibility to novel strains in different age groups, thereby contributing to a protective or risk I0 profile if the HA subtype is a match or mismatch to the imprinting strain, respectively.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors based on the concept of antigenic imprinting.

claim: A memory T cell pool that is smaller in size, non-cross-reactive, narrow in repertoire diversity, or inappropriately targeted will contribute to a risk I0 profile.
source: A memory T cell pool that is smaller in size, non-cross-reactive, narrow in repertoire diversity, or inappropriately targeted (with respect to immunodominance hierarchy) will contribute to a risk I0 profile.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors about how memory T cell characteristics affect I0.

claim: The memory T cell pool, and thus I0, can be tailored to confer optimal protection, provided the appropriate priming strain is selected.
source: However, the memory T cell pool, and thus I0, can be tailored to confer optimal protection, provided the appropriate priming strain is selected.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors about the potential to manipulate I0 through vaccination.

claim: TRM would likely be enriched in protective I0 profiles for respiratory infections through rapid initiation of immunity and augmented viral clearance.
source: Of note, inclusion of TRM into I0 calculations (discussed in 'Implementing I0' section) will be limited by the difficulty in obtaining human tissue samples, as opposed to blood, which is easily collected and less invasive. However, in unique experimental designs for which this is possible, TRM would likely be enriched in protective I0 profiles for respiratory infections through rapid initiation of immunity and augmented viral clearance.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors based on the known functions of TRM cells.

claim: Race and ethnicity categories are dynamic, subjective, and shaped by changing social and geopolitical forces.
source: Ethnicity is defined by social and cultural norms, whereas race is determined by physical characteristics (Mersha and Abebe, 2015). These categories are dynamic, subjective, and shaped by changing social and geopolitical forces.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mersha and Abebe, 2015.

evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the definition of ancestry.

claim: Biases in study recruitment limit our understanding of health and disease, and impairs the ability to effectively treat patients.
source: Biases in study recruitment, at the basic science and clinical trials level, limit our understanding of health and disease, and, most importantly, impairs the ability to effectively treat patients.
evidence: This is stated as a general principle about the impact of recruitment biases.

source: Moreover, implementation of tools based on studies with biased demographics, particularly ancestry, can exacerbate health disparities (Carson et al., 1999; Martin et al., 2019).

claim: Increasing diversity in study population composition presents statistical challenges but is imperative to detect influencing factors unique to distinct groups, de-couple correlated variables, understand all pathophysiologies underlying disease, and design broadly applicable, effective therapeutics.
source: Although increasing diversity in study population composition, both genetic and socio-culture, presents statistical challenges, it is imperative in order to: (1) detect influencing factors that may be unique to distinct groups, (2) de-couple correlated variables within populations, (3) understand all pathophysiologies underlying disease, and (4) design broadly applicable, effective therapeutics (De Jager et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to De Jager et al., 2015.
